title: Classified Employees Reduction In Force - Lack of Funds and/or Lack of Work - 2022-2023 Fiscal Year - Talent/Human Resources Department
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0122 - Classified Employees Reduction In Force Due to Lack of Funds and/or Lack of Work 2022-2023 Fiscal Year.
headline: Board votes on laying off classified staff for 2022-23 because of lack of funds or work
summary: This resolution would authorize a reduction in force, which means layoffs, of classified employees for the 2022-2023 fiscal year, citing lack of funds and/or lack of work. Classified employees are district staff who are not teachers or administrators. The text does not say which positions or how many are affected.
pulled_from_consent: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (5–2), instead of with the rest of the consent report.

title: Temporary Hiring Freeze – School Sites and Central Office Positions – Talent/Human Resources Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0123 - Temporary Hiring Freeze - School Sites and Central Office Positions [Effective January 27, 2022].
headline: Freezes hiring for school-site and central office positions starting January 27, 2022
summary: This resolution puts a temporary hiring freeze in place for positions at school sites and in the central office. It takes effect January 27, 2022. The text does not say how long the freeze lasts.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Emma Donnelly - East Oakland Pride Elementary School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Emma Donnelly, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide English as Second Language (ESL) classes to 25-30 parents, twice per week for 16 weeks at East Oakland Pride Elementary School, for the period of January 24, 2022, through March 25, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $2,500.00.
headline: Ratifies $2,500 for English classes for parents at East Oakland Pride Elementary
summary: The district would pay a contractor up to $2,500 to teach English as a Second Language classes to 25-30 parents, twice a week for 16 weeks, at East Oakland Pride Elementary School. The service period is January 24 to March 25, 2022, and the work began before the board's approval. The money comes from Title I, a federal grant for low-income students.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Subcontract - Spanish Speaking Unity Council of Alameda County, Inc. - General Child Care and Development Programs - Early Childhood Education
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0106 - Authorizing Subcontract to the Spanish Speaking Unity Council of Alameda County, Inc., dba The Unity Council, a Portion of District's Fiscal Year 2021-22 Child Development Funding [for the period of July 1, 2021, through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $400,000.00].
funding_source: General Child Development Program CCTR Grant
headline: Approves up to $400,000 for The Unity Council to run child care and development programs
summary: The board would pass a portion of the district's 2021-22 state child development funding, up to $400,000, to the Spanish Speaking Unity Council of Alameda County (doing business as The Unity Council) through a subcontract. The period is July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022. It is part of the district's early childhood education programs.
vendor_name: Spanish Speaking Unity Council of Alameda County, Inc. (The Unity Council)
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Subcontract - YMCA of the East Bay - General Child Care and Development Programs - Early Childhood Education
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0104 - Authorizing Subcontract to the YMCA of the East Bay, a Portion of District's Fiscal Year 2021-22 Child Development Funding [for the period of October 1, 2021, through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $200,000.00].
headline: Approves up to $200,000 for the YMCA of the East Bay to run child care and development programs

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Spearitwurx - Office of Equity
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Spearitwurx, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide Equity and Wellness Engagement pre and post-assessment for teachers and staff (plus… review available data for students and families); site visit and consultation with designated … Consultant and school site administrative team, lead teachers and/or staff to determine school-specific equity needs; facilitation of 5-7 customized professional engagement sessions - (can be done in no less than 90- minute blocks - total of 15 hours of direct facilitation) and customized Equity and Wellness kits for participating staff 1-on-1 and group-coaching sessions for selected staff (as needed), via the Office of Equity, for the period of January 3, 2022 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $97,500.00.
headline: Pays Spearitwurx up to $97,500 for equity and wellness work with school staff
summary: The district would pay Spearitwurx, an Oakland provider, up to $97,500 through the Office of Equity. The work includes staff assessments, school site visits, 5-7 customized sessions (15 hours in total), wellness kits and coaching for selected staff. The service period is January 3 to June 30, 2022, which began before the January 26 board meeting.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Student Travel - College and University Campuses Tour - Eugene, Oregon - Castlemont High School
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0156 - Authorization for Approval of Student Travel by school site Castlemont High School, for 12 students and 3 adults, as specified in Out of State Field Trip/Excursion Request, attached, to volunteer with Habitat for Humanity, and to travel and tour the college campuses of Bushnell University, Lane Community College, and the University of Oregon, Eugene, Oregon, for the period of January 31, 2022 through February 4, 2022, at no cost to the District.
headline: Approves Castlemont High trip to Oregon college campuses at no cost to the district
summary: Castlemont High School would take 12 students and 3 adults to Eugene, Oregon, from January 31 to February 4, 2022. They would volunteer with Habitat for Humanity and tour Bushnell University, Lane Community College and the University of Oregon. The trip costs the district nothing.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: District "Brown Act" Legislative Bodies - February 2022 - Virtual Meetings - Board of Education
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0014D - Making Certain Findings Necessary To Permit Virtual Meetings In Specified Circumstances for February 2022.
headline: Allows board and district committees to keep meeting virtually in February 2022
summary: This resolution makes the findings state law requires so that the board and other district public bodies subject to the Brown Act (California's open meeting law) can hold virtual meetings during February 2022. It involves no spending.
pulled_from_consent: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (4–3), instead of with the rest of the consent report.

title: Charter Schools Facilities Request - Finding/Reasons - Charter Schools Could Not Be Accommodated - Single Site - School Year 2022-2023 - Charter Schools Office
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0155 - Finding That Charter Schools Cannot Be Accommodated At A Single Site And Written Statement Of Reasons Explaining The Finding.

·	for 44,704 square feet: 2022-23 Proposition 39 per square foot rate during the 2022-23 Fiscal Year*; and 1.05 times the 2023-24 Proposition 39 per square foot rate during the 2023-24 Fiscal Year.
